resolved_decisions.D23: RESOLVED 2026-07-27 — a file's raw mirror is that file's last unit; at most one per file. Seal-side construction rule; parse position-agnostic.
resolved_decisions.D28: RESOLVED 2026-07-28 — full-reveal strictness is STRICT (hard-fail): a bundle revealing every kind=Normal unit of a file MUST carry that file's file_salt, plus s_root iff the file has a fine tree. Rider 1 (binding on F8): reveal shape is DERIVED from the signed unit table and the revealed set, NEVER declared — the bundle carries no reveal-shape discriminant. docs/decisions/D28-full-reveal-strictness.md
resolved_decisions.D77: RESOLVED 2026-07-28 — a zero-non-mirror-unit (mirror-only) file is REJECTED at F5 (manifest schema), code manifest-empty-normal-units via ContainerField::NormalUnits, checked in FileEntry::new AFTER the units.is_empty() check and BEFORE the coverage loop. This DOES change the registry, correcting the fed_but_not_resolved_here note that assumed otherwise: maps.file_entry key 6 gains 'at least one kind=normal unit [P]'. D28's anti-vacuity clause and C7's attest refusal stay as defence-in-depth (R's view types are hand-populated, so no F5 check can constrain them). docs/decisions/D77-zero-unit-file.md
resolved_decisions.D10: RESOLVED 2026-07-28 — 19 frozen parser resource caps, one universal clamp rule min(claimed_length, remaining_input) applied at every pre-allocation whether or not a cap covers it, 18 new bundle-/manifest- codes plus the existing cbor-nesting-too-deep; all enforced inside verify stage 1 (decode), ahead of every AEAD, hash and signature operation; u64 everywhere so wasm32 and native cannot diverge. resolved_decisions.D74: RESOLVED 2026-07-28 — an extraneous s_root on a FineTree::Absent full reveal is REJECTED, code full-reveal-s-root-without-fine-tree, tier R (it needs the manifest descriptor and the derived predicate). One code, not a pair: the FileSalt counterpart is unreachable because full_reveal key 1 is required at schema level, so F8 rejects a key-1-less entry as bundle-missing-key before R4 runs. Mirrored on maps.full_reveal.violations[4]. docs/decisions/D74-extraneous-full-reveal-s-root.md
resolved_decisions.D75: RESOLVED 2026-07-28 — a full reveal ships per-unit covers AND s_root: covered_reveal key 3 is unconditionally required at tier P. The s_root-only reading would have made the key's presence depend on the derived full-reveal predicate, moving it from P to R, which D78 forbids the bundle schema layer from deciding. Rider: the two routes to fine_root must be required to AGREE. Correction 1 (applied to registry-v1.md section 7.11 at the freeze): the s_root rebuild does NOT prove 'no extra leaves' — both routes take the leaf count from the same place — it is defence-in-depth for content binding AND the sole consumer of the disclosed s_root itself. docs/decisions/D75-full-reveal-cover-shape.md
resolved_decisions.D76: RESOLVED 2026-07-28 — NO file_salt split for v1: one 16-byte file_salt salts both raw_commit and canon_commit (MVP-SPEC.md line 95). Both salts' presence would have become tier R, making a full_reveal entry undecidable at F8 (D78). A future raw_salt takes a reserved slot of maps.full_reveal, never displaces key 1. Mirrored on maps.full_reveal key 1 and in registry-v1.md section 7.14. docs/decisions/D76-file-salt-split.md
resolved_decisions.D78: RATIFIED 2026-07-28 — bundle schema validation NEVER consults the embedded manifest. F8 decides the bundle from the bundle's own bytes; any rule needing both sides is tier R, never a schema error. Enforced structurally rather than by assertion: BundleError has no arm that can carry a ManifestError. This fixes which error family every cross-side rejection lands in, and D30 makes error codes permanent. Mirrored in validation_tiers.ratified_rule and registry-v1.md sections 0 and 7.6.3.
resolved_decisions.D79: RATIFIED 2026-07-28 — the OTS upgrade group (ots_anchor keys 2-4) is FREE-STANDING all-or-nothing: its presence is never conditioned on status. status is sealer-written and the design requires a verifier not to trust it; conditioning a PARSE rule on it would let a sealer choose which shapes decode — the same derived-not-declared principle D28 rider 1 applies to reveal shape. Consequence accepted deliberately: status = pending with height + header is well-formed v1, and what status values MEAN is A-domain semantics at M2. Failure: BundleError::OtsUpgradeGroupIncomplete. Mirrored on maps.ots_anchor.presence_groups[0].
resolved_decisions.D80: RESOLVED 2026-07-28 — every revealed unit's owning file MUST have a touched_files entry, tier R, code revealed-unit-file-not-touched. R and not X because a unit's OWNING FILE is a manifest fact (the unit table is nested inside file entries), which D78 forbids the bundle schema layer from reaching for. Evidence: MVP-SPEC.md line 95 (path_salt ships whenever any reveal TOUCHES the file) and line 121 (only two rendering states). docs/decisions/D80-revealed-unit-touched-file.md
resolved_decisions.D82: RESOLVED 2026-07-28 — the converse of D80: every touched_files entry must belong to a file with a revealed unit. REJECT, tier R, code touched-file-without-revealed-unit (R5 coherence group 1b). Together with D80 the two state an EQUALITY — touched_files names exactly the files with a revealed unit — and neither subsumes the X rule full_reveals-subset-of-touched_files. Line 121 does not merely omit 'unrevealed file, path disclosed'; it states the opposite. Absent from this registry until the Q14 freeze. docs/decisions/D82-touched-file-without-reveal.md
resolved_decisions.D84: RESOLVED 2026-07-28 — the internal structural limits of the opaque anchor artifacts (.ots op counts, DER nesting, signed-attribute counts) are NOT v1 format surface and do NOT freeze at Q14: they are set at M2 against A25's real artifacts. What does freeze is the anchor ENVELOPE (maps.ots_anchor, maps.tsa_anchor) and D10's caps over it. Recorded here because caps.not_in_scope previously pointed this question at D83, which is the leaf-level GGM payload — an inherited number collision. docs/decisions/D84-anchor-artifact-limits-permanence.md
resolved_decisions.D83: RESOLVED 2026-07-28 — canonical leaf-level GGM payload; option B. A disclosed GGM payload at level == d is salt_i || 0x00*16; the length stays 32 and stays tier P, and the zero tail is a tier R value rule. BINDS: cover_entry element 2 at level == d (section 5, section 7.11 key 3), and full_reveal key 2 at n == 1 (section 7.14), where d == 0 makes the grid root itself a leaf. One new code, fine-root-leaf-seed-tail-not-zero, surfaced from both sites; no CBOR type, length, key assignment or reserved slot changes, so format_version stays 1. Mirrored on the cover_entry tuple's element 2 and on full_reveal key 2 as `canonical_leaf_payload`, and in registry-v1.md sections 2, 5, 7.11 and 7.14. docs/decisions/D83-leaf-cover-seed-tail-malleability.md

validation_tiers.ratified_rule: bundle schema validation never consults the embedded manifest (D78, ratified 2026-07-28)

tiers.decidable_from: bundle plus embedded manifest, or crypto

decode_layers.zero_copy_requirement: layer 2 must receive a sub-slice of the bundle input, never a copy: Manifest's guarantee that work_id and signature pre-images are the received bytes holds by construction only for a borrowed slice

max_container_depth.cap_basis: max of the two, not the sum — layer 2 starts a fresh decoder over the bstr contents
max_container_depth.note: cap frozen by D10 as MAX_CBOR_DEPTH = 8 = 6 + 2, leaving room for one additive v1.x field nested one level deeper; see the top-level `caps` object

discriminants.read_after: nothing — first key of the file

version_dispatch.envelope_frozen_across_versions: the manifest body's discriminant sits INSIDE the body bstr, so the {body, signatures} envelope must be parsed before the version is readable at all; it therefore can never carry a version-specific change, and has no reserved band and no discriminant of its own (§1 rule 6, §7.1)
version_dispatch.discriminants_are_independent: a v1 bundle may one day carry a v2 manifest; the two rejections are separate codes in separate families (D78) and must stay separable
version_dispatch.unsupported_is_not_malformed: an unrowed version yields the version error and NOTHING else — never a canonicality error and never an unknown/reserved-key error, even when the rest of the artifact would also fail v1 validation. A *missing* discriminant is `*-missing-key`; a non-canonical one is the `cbor-*` class.
version_dispatch.constant_cost_peek: canonical maps ascend (§1 rule 3), so key 0 is first on the wire whenever present and the version peek is constant-cost in artifact size — an unsupported oversized artifact is rejected before any section is walked, earlier than the F11 caps apply
version_dispatch.released_versions_decodable_forever: MVP-SPEC.md line 123: support is added by appending a row to the dispatch table, never by widening an older version's decoder

checked_absences.note: F8's checklist test asserts these are absent, rather than merely not implementing them

items.reason: nonces come from the manifest — single source of truth (MVP-SPEC.md line 114)

items.absent: any signature container at bundle level
items.reason: the bundle is unsigned; authority is the embedded signed manifest plus the anchor artifacts. Signing the bundle would invite trusting the assembler, who is the sealer (line 121)

items.absent: work_id / anchor_digest / seal_id at bundle level
items.reason: all derived; a stored copy could contradict the bytes it summarizes
positional — bundle key 3 is OTS, key 4 is TSA (section 7.6.2); the illegal cross-placement is unrepresentable

items.absent: any reveal-shape discriminant (is_full_reveal, reveal_mode, reveal_shape) at any level
items.reason: D28 rider 1 — reveal shape is DERIVED from the signed unit table and the revealed set. A declared shape is sealer-forgeable: declaring 'partial' while revealing every unit would smuggle back the permissive full-reveal option D28 rejected. BINDING CONSTRAINT ON F8 — do not add this field

items.absent: a TSA source string on tsa_anchor (removed from v1 by D8 section 1)
items.reason: a sealer's claim about an anchor's PROVENANCE, bound by nothing — the bundle is unsigned, so any relay can rewrite it undetectably — and consumed by nothing: verify/pipeline.rs refuses to copy bundle-recorded anchor metadata into the report, in writing. A verdict's source identity comes from the verified certificate chain against the pinned root store (MVP-SPEC.md line 109) for TSA and from the .ots attestations for OTS. It was also the only assigned key in v1 with no spec basis at all. Key 4 is now plain reserved and its presence raises F10's ordinary reserved-slot error

items.absent: any chain identifier (chain_id, network name) in receipt_record
items.reason: the chain is PINNED BY THE VERIFIER (MVP-SPEC.md line 137: two public Arbitrum RPCs, user-overridable), never named by the artifact under inspection. A sealer-written chain_id would steer the verifier's RPC choice — the same hazard as a bundle-side nonce or a bundle-supplied trust root (line 109: bundle-embedded chains supply intermediates only). A receipt captured on Sepolia or a devnet simply fails to resolve against Arbitrum One at v1.1, which is the correct outcome and stronger than trusting the bundle to admit it

profile.encoding: RFC 8949 section 4.2.1 Core Deterministic (MVP-SPEC.md line 73; minicbor =2.3.0 per D7)
profile.key_error_bands: unassigned key in 0..=23 -> reserved-slot error naming the key; key >= 24 -> unknown-key error (F10)
profile.magic_bytes: none — version discriminant is map key 0, first in canonical encoded order

caps.enforcement_point: verify stage 1 (decode) — every cap fires before any AEAD, hash, or signature work
caps.wasm32_parity: every byte/count cap is u64 and <= u32::MAX, so each is reachable and compares identically on wasm32 and native; MAX_CBOR_DEPTH is the deliberate u16 exception (it counts containers, never wire lengths)
caps.clamp_rule: every pre-allocation clamped to min(claimed_length, remaining_input); order at an array head is head canonicality -> cap -> clamped allocation -> elements
caps.recorded_non_caps: sig_policy / pubkeys / signatures (bounded by the 16-value registered sig_alg universe of section 6.2 and by duplicate-freedom, so an existing code fires first — which is why that universe is frozen twice over, by section 6.2 and by this row); range / cover_entry / path_node (fixed arity); title / app_version / touched_file.path (free-form tstr, transitively bounded by caps 1-2); revealed-unit ciphertext (already shape-checked; an upper bound would equal MAX_BUNDLE_BYTES). The clamp rule still applies to every one of them.
caps.not_in_scope: internal structural limits of the opaque artifacts (.ots op counts, DER nesting, signed-attribute counts) are A's at M2 (sections 7.8, 7.9; MVP-SPEC.md line 153) — their freeze status is decision D84: NOT v1 format surface, so they do not freeze at Q14. The anchor envelope and D10's caps over it do.

presence_groups.name: upgrade_group
presence_groups.rule: all-or-nothing: an upgraded OTS anchor carries height + header + fetch date together; a not-yet-upgraded one carries none. Two of three present is malformed
presence_groups.free_standing: RATIFIED 2026-07-28 — the group's presence is NEVER conditioned on status. status is sealer-written and the design requires a verifier not to trust it; conditioning a parse rule on it would let a sealer choose which shapes decode. Consequence accepted deliberately: status = pending with height + header is well-formed v1

fields.name: status
fields.notes: enum anchor_status; sealer-recorded, never trusted — the verifier derives its own state

fields.name: ots
fields.notes: raw .ots, opaque at this layer (A parses)

fields.name: block_height
fields.notes: attested Bitcoin block height

fields.name: block_header
fields.notes: exactly 80 bytes (line 108); a wrong length is its own error, never a malformed-header error

fields.name: fetch_date
fields.notes: POSIX seconds; the instant the sealer COMPLETED THE UPGRADE CAPTURE — obtained the attested block height AND the 80-byte header and wrote them to the journal. NOT the .ots submission time (not carried anywhere) and NOT the Bitcoin block timestamp, which lives inside the embedded header and is the datum --online confirmation promotes to proven (line 108). Membership in the upgrade group is what makes this the only coherent reading: a not-yet-upgraded anchor has no upgrade to have fetched. Three non-rules: no ordering relation to the header timestamp or to claimed_time, no bounds, no monotonicity. Privacy: it reveals when the sealer last ran the CLI. D8 section 4b

maps.name: tsa_anchor
maps.doc: MVP-SPEC.md lines 109/112-114. DER token and certificates are opaque bstrs here; CMS/X.509 parsing, pinned-root chain validation and valid-at-stamping evaluation are A's, at M2

fields.name: status
fields.notes: enum anchor_status; sealer-recorded, never trusted

fields.name: token
fields.notes: DER TimeStampResp/token, opaque at this layer

fields.name: intermediates
fields.notes: bstr DER certs; intermediates ONLY — a bundle-supplied chain can never close against a bundle-supplied root (line 109), so no root slot exists here to be tempted by

fields.name: fetch_date
fields.notes: POSIX seconds; the instant the sealer RECEIVED the TimeStampResp — NOT the token's genTime, which is inside the DER and is the provable time (MVP-SPEC.md line 109). Always known at seal, hence required where the OTS counterpart is optional. Three non-rules bind it: no ordering relation to genTime or claimed_time, no bounds (zero is legal), no monotonicity across the list

reserved.purpose: future v1.x fields. Key 4 previously held an informational `source` tstr, REMOVED from v1 by D8 section 1 and now a checked absence: it is plain reserved, not a named slot, because a TSA source string is committed to nothing. Assigning it in a later v1.x release is the ordinary additive path

maps.name: receipt_record
maps.doc: MVP-SPEC.md line 110; opt-in; payload internals A/S-owned and deliberately outside this registry. MVP verdict is fixed at 'supporting evidence — no independently proven time' and no reserved slot can promote it

fields.name: tx_hashes
fields.notes: bstr(32) Keccak-256 EVM tx hashes; non-empty; capture order

fields.name: block_number
fields.notes: the Arbitrum One block number of the EARLIEST-CONFIRMED transaction in key 0 — the MINIMUM block number over the receipt's transactions. A payment may span several transactions (S1 section 12: at most 256 transfers per tx, one TxHash per sub-batch), each confirmed in its own block, so 'the payment's block' is DEFINED, not observed; the drafted wording named nothing and two honest implementations would have picked differently. Display-only: unverified in v1, never verdict-bearing, re-derivable from any transaction hash over RPC. A per-transaction structure, if a consumer ever needs one, takes a reserved key additively and must then be per-tx, never a second scalar (D8 section 3b)

fields.name: payload
fields.notes: opaque A/S serialization: quote preimages + proof_bytes (the v1.1-chain capture). Opaque to this registry — its internal layout is not a v1 wire format, so its contents may change in any release without a format-version event and without a reseal. Nothing in a v1 verdict may depend on its internal structure. Capture COMPLETENESS is an S-domain obligation (S7) with no freeze deadline, because the vault rather than the bundle is what a reseal would rebuild from; anything v1.1 must read in a version-stable, cross-implementation way is promoted into reserved key 3 (D8 section 3a)

reserved.name: chain_inputs
reserved.purpose: v1.1 Arbitrum-receipt verification chain (spec line 161: address recomputation <-> quote preimages <-> tx calldata) — the slot into which v1.1 may promote registry-visible, version-stable structure out of the opaque payload. Needed because key 2 is deliberately outside this registry, so anything the WASM page and the CLI must read identically under the line-123 stability contract cannot live there. Reject-if-present in v1

maps.name: covered_reveal
maps.doc: MVP-SPEC.md lines 96/112-114 per revealed fine-tree-covered unit. Carries no nonce (manifest is the single source) and no AAD (reconstructed from manifest seal_id + this entry's unit_id, line 91). cover/paths are NESTED inside the reveal they belong to, so a proof reaching outside the revealed set is unrepresentable in v1 — BundleView.proof_unit_refs idles until bundle key 10 is assigned in v1.1

fields.name: unit_id
fields.notes: must resolve into the embedded manifest's unit table

fields.name: k_u
fields.notes: the unit key, disclosed per reveal so the verifier decrypts without ever holding W (line 114). No LengthField class — R binds keys by whether they decrypt, not by length

fields.name: ciphertext
fields.notes: len % 256 == 16 and len >= 272 at parse; the exact len == padded_length(true_length)+16 is R's (needs the manifest)

fields.name: cover
fields.rule: D75 RESOLVED 2026-07-28 with F8: BOTH — unconditionally required, including for units of a fully revealed file whose full_reveal entry also carries s_root. The s_root-only reading would have made this key's presence depend on the derived full-reveal predicate, moving it from tier P to tier R, which D78 forbids the bundle schema layer from deciding. Rider: the two routes to fine_root must be required to AGREE (open tamper row for R4/Q8)
fields.notes: cover_entry tuples; non-empty (a covered unit has >= 1 leaf; the empty unit is never covered); strictly ascending leaf-interval start [X]; leaf-exactness and no-ancestor-seed are R's

fields.name: paths
fields.notes: path_node tuples; strictly ascending leaf-interval start; empty exactly when the unit spans [0, n) — the 'exactly' is R's

maps.name: noncovered_reveal
maps.doc: MVP-SPEC.md lines 92/94/112-114 per revealed non-covered unit (--no-fine-tree or raw-mirror) — the two cases bound by unit_commit rather than fine_root (line 94). Keys 0-2 are deliberately key-aligned with covered_reveal so both reveal kinds share one decode prefix. A raw-mirror reveal is an ordinary entry here: no mirror flag, no link field — the manifest's kind identifies it

fields.name: unit_id
fields.notes: resolves into the manifest unit table; whether a unit legitimately belongs in THIS array rather than covered_reveal is also R's

fields.name: ciphertext
fields.notes: same parse shape check as covered_reveal.ciphertext

fields.name: unit_salt
fields.notes: opens unit_commit = SHA-256(0x02 || unit_salt || bytes) (line 94)

maps.name: touched_file
maps.doc: MVP-SPEC.md lines 112-114 per touched file; explicit file_id decided YES (registry-v1.md section 10). path_salt is the path-only salt, independent of file_salt precisely so naming a file never weakens its content commitments (line 95) — the two must never be merged in a future version

fields.name: file_id
fields.notes: index into the embedded manifest's file table; in-range

fields.name: path
fields.notes: the tstr's bytes AS RECEIVED are the commitment pre-image: path_commit = SHA-256(0x05 || path_salt || path_utf8) (line 95). No NFC, no separator rewriting, no case folding — the text canonicalization pipeline (D20/D21) governs file CONTENT, never this field

maps.name: full_reveal
maps.doc: MVP-SPEC.md lines 112-114/121 per fully-revealed file. D28 (resolved 2026-07-28) makes this section's presence a BICONDITIONAL over a DERIVED predicate, not a sealer option: an entry exists for file F iff full(F). The entry is material, not a claim — its presence must AGREE with the independently derived predicate, and there is no reveal-shape field anywhere to declare it

derived_predicate.N_of_F: unit_ids of manifest units with file_id = F and kind = Normal
load_bearing_clauses: kind = Normal only — raw-mirror units are exempt by kind, never by position (D23); a mirror-only reveal is partial
N(F) != empty (anti-vacuity, D77) — otherwise a hand-built zero-unit file is vacuously full for every bundle, including one revealing nothing
s_root conditional on FineTree::Present — a --no-fine-tree or empty file has none

violations.notes: realized as a MISSING ENTRY, not an entry with a missing key: key 1 is required at schema level, so F8 rejects a key-1-less entry as a schema error before R4 runs

violations.condition: full(F) and fine_tree Present, key 2 absent
full(F) and fine_tree Absent, key 2 present
violations.notes: D74 RESOLVED 2026-07-28 with F8: reject (docs/decisions/D74-extraneous-full-reveal-s-root.md). One code, not a FullRevealMaterial pair — the FileSalt counterpart is unreachable because key 1 is required at schema level, so F8 rejects a key-1-less entry as bundle-missing-key before R4 runs. The check itself is R4's: it needs the manifest descriptor and the derived predicate

fields.name: file_id
fields.notes: in-range (R); must also appear in touched_files (X)

fields.name: file_salt
fields.notes: opens raw_commit/canon_commit; disclosed ONLY on a full reveal (line 95)

fields.name: s_root
fields.rule: biconditional [R]: present iff full(F) AND file fine_tree == Present
fields.notes: full [0, n) cover; discloses nothing since every leaf is revealed (line 114)
fields.canonical_leaf_payload: at n == 1 (d == 0) the grid root is a leaf, so this field is salt_0 || 0x00*16 and a non-zero upper half is rejected (D83, tier R)
